Subject: Competitive eval — model quality follow-up (Acme Corp)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from the call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: validate model quality regressions and hallucination characteristics for the 3 core workflows you highlighted (customer support summarization, knowledge-grounded Q&A, and product content generation).
- Baseline comparison: your internal runs vs Hyperscaler-A API (v4) and Hyperscaler-B (latest).
- Redwood asks: a) share the eval prompts and any known failure modes, b) allow us to run the same prompts through our inference with the exact model variants you want tested (we recommend the open-variant + our quantized config), c) collect hallucination and factuality metrics.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You upload the eval prompts + examples (we created a CSV template, see attachment).
2) We run a 2-day regression pass and share a detailed comparison matrix and sample outputs.
3) If we see regressions, we iterate on prompt engineering + model variant suggestion; if hallucination is the issue, we test retrieval augmentation and our hallucination-penalty prompts.

Can you confirm the ownership for the prompt upload (Alice or Ben)? Also what SLA do you need for turnaround (48 hours OK)?

I attached a CSV template for the prompts and an initial comparison matrix we use internally. We'll include Aditya on any contract/discount asks if the evaluation expands.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-eval-prompts.csv]
[Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx]

Subject: Re: Competitive eval — model quality follow-up (Acme Corp)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. That all sounds good. Ben will own the prompt export and upload — Ben, can you drop the CSV into the Drive folder by EOD Tuesday? Our internal expectation is a 48–72 hour turnaround given the size of the evaluator set (~1,200 prompts).

A few clarifications from our side:
- For the baseline, we're using Hyperscaler-A v4 with default sampling and Hyperscaler-B with temperature=0.2.
- We definitely want hallucination rate broken out by intent (e.g., policy queries vs. product facts) — that's critical for our compliance team.
- Please include a short CSV column indicating which prompts are "must-pass" (critical).

One ask: can Redwood also run a small batch with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) using our internal product index? We can provide a read-only S3/endpoint for that test.

Thanks — looking forward to the comparison.

Best,
Alice
Director, AI Products
Acme Corp

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks — that timeline works. A few updates and confirmations from our side: 

1) Prompt upload: Ben — use this Drive folder (we created a subfolder for Acme tests): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cacme-evals. I'll confirm ingestion when it's there. Please include the "must-pass" column as Alice requested.

2) RAG test: yes — we can run a RAG pass. Please share the read-only S3 endpoint and an IAM role with limited access (or a signed URL). We'll isolate the RAG runs to a dedicated experiment.

3) Test plan and metrics: we'll run the same prompts across three configs: your Hyperscaler baseline (as you described), Redwood default open-variant (quantized), and Redwood + retrieval. We'll measure: factuality/hallucination rate, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and a per-intent confusion/hallucination breakdown. Expect the preliminary matrix in ~48 hours after we have the prompts. The deliverable will include: sample outputs, per-prompt deltas vs baseline, and a short list of remediation recommendations.

4) Attachments: attaching our prompt CSV template and an internal regression-report example so you know the format.

5) Commercials: Aditya — looping you in. If Acme wants a dedicated 5-day extended eval or an SLA-backed pilot, what's our typical pricing guidance?

Next steps: Ben uploads prompts -> we run first pass (48 hours) -> share matrix -> sync call to review findings and remediation.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
